welcome.title: Prepare the installation files
welcome.lead: Select a deployment method and enter the site domain. Some methods require creating the site and completing SSL first. Secrets and image versions are filled in automatically.
welcome.note: This tool only generates configuration files and does not modify the server.
panel.title: Select a deployment method
panel.lead: Choose the panel, compose UI, or outer reverse proxy already in use. If Docker is used directly, select Command line.
panel.1panel.desc: Paste YAML into Compose and .env into environment variables
panel.baota.desc: Paste the compose file, or place the files in the site directory
panel.generic.desc: Start with docker compose from the command line
panel.1panel.wizardHint: After generation, paste the YAML into Compose and the .env into environment variables.
panel.baota.wizardHint: After generation, paste the compose file, or place both files in the same directory.
panel.generic.wizardHint: After generation, place both files in the same directory and run docker compose up -d.
panel.baota.composeBadge: Paste YAML or deploy from a directory
panel.baota.label: Baota panel
panel.generic.label: Generic / CLI
panel.1panel.siteStep3: Drop the site configuration file below
panel.1panel.siteConfPath: The file may also be found under the site directory or OpenResty conf.d as {domain}.conf
panel.1panel.resultsIntro: Paste docker-compose.yml into Containers / Compose, and paste .env into environment variables. The site must reverse-proxy the entire host to the local port.
panel.baota.siteStep2: Request SSL in the site settings
panel.baota.siteStep3: Drop the site configuration file below
panel.baota.resultsIntro: Create a compose project and paste the YAML, or place compose and .env in the same directory. For the bundled database, read the directory permission notes first.
panel.generic.siteStep3: Drop the existing Nginx configuration below
panel.generic.resultsIntro: Place docker-compose.yml and .env in the same directory, run docker compose up -d, then reverse-proxy the entire site from the outer Nginx.
domain.title: Site domain
domain.lead: Myriad will be reached at this address. Do not include https://.
domain.extraHint: Leave empty if none is required
site.title: Prepare the site and certificate
site.lead: Create the site and complete SSL first, then upload the existing .conf. Certificate settings are kept where possible; only a full-site reverse proxy is applied.
site.noDomain: Return to the previous step and enter a domain first.
site.noFile: If no file is uploaded, a default configuration is generated. Certificates must be added later.
db.title: Choose a database deployment
db.lead: The bundled PostgreSQL is recommended for a first install. Choose external if an instance is already available.
db.bundledDesc: Deployed with the compose stack; no separate database setup
db.externalDesc: Enter the connection details of an existing database
db.bundledHint: The database name, user, and password are written automatically.
db.name: Database name
db.extraNetworkHint: Required only when the database and Myriad are not on the same Docker network. A common 1Panel value is 1panel-network.
db.passwordPlaceholder: Enter the password of the external database
limits.title: Resource limits
limits.lead: Choose limits that match the available server resources. Use the recommended profile if unsure.
limits.hintSmall: Small: database 0.5 CPU / 512M, backend 1 CPU / 1G, frontend 0.5 CPU / 256M. Memory saver is enabled automatically.
limits.hintStandard: Recommended: database 1 CPU / 1G, backend 2 CPU / 2G, frontend 1 CPU / 512M.
limits.hintLarge: Generous: database 2 CPU / 2G, backend 2 CPU / 2G, frontend 1 CPU / 1G.
limits.hintCustom: Enter CPU and memory for each service. Memory values look like 512M or 2G.
limits.dbDesc: Used by the bundled PostgreSQL. This container is omitted for an external database.
advanced.title: Advanced options
advanced.lead: The defaults are ready for production. Generate now unless a special setup is required.
advanced.memorySaverDesc: Tightens caches, connection pools, and federation concurrency. Enabled automatically for the Small profile.
done.title: Complete the deployment in this order
done.lead: Save the setup secret first, then place the files as described for the selected panel.
done.secretBody: It is required when the site is first opened and the owner account is created. The install link can also be copied; the wizard fills it in automatically.
guide.generic.placeTitle: Place the files in one directory and start
guide.generic.placeBody: Create a directory on the server, add docker-compose.yml and .env, then run the command.
guide.generic.proxyBody: Place the generated {domain}.conf in Nginx and reverse-proxy the entire site to {bind}. Do not proxy /api only.
guide.baota.pasteTitle: Paste the compose file into Baota
guide.baota.pasteBody: Open Baota → Docker → Compose → Create, paste docker-compose.yml, and place .env in the same directory.
guide.baota.overwriteBody: Open Baota Websites → Settings → Configuration and overwrite it with the generated {domain}.conf. The proxy target is {bind} and must cover the entire site /.
guide.1panel.pasteBody: Open 1Panel → Containers → Compose → Create. Paste docker-compose.yml as YAML and the full .env as environment variables.
guide.1panel.overwriteBody: Open 1Panel Websites → Configuration and overwrite it with the generated {domain}.conf. The target is http://{bind} and must reverse-proxy the entire site.
guide.openTitle: Open the site and create the owner
guide.openBody: After the containers are up, open the install link. The wizard fills in the secret automatically.
notify.noSecret: No setup secret has been generated yet
notify.noLink: No install link has been generated yet
notify.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select the text and copy it manually.
notify.generated: Configuration generated. Copy the setup secret first; it is required when creating the owner.
notify.tagsAligned: Updated to the shared Docker Hub versioned tag
notify.tagsMixed: Tags updated (proxy / updater may differ from the application version)
notify.tagsFailed: Failed to fetch the latest versions: {message}
error.badMainDomain: The primary domain is not valid
error.badExtraDomain: The additional domain is not valid
error.badDbName: The database name may contain only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, and must start with a letter
error.badDbUser: The database username may contain only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, and must start with a letter
error.badDbHost: Enter a valid database host (IP / hostname / host.docker.internal)
error.badDbPort: The database port is not valid
error.badExtraNetwork: The additional network is not a valid Docker network name
error.badHttpBind: The HTTP listen address is not valid
error.badHttpPort: The HTTP port is not valid
error.badPgVersion: The PostgreSQL major version must be an integer from {min} to {max} (current image line)
error.emptyTags: Image tags are empty and could not be resolved. Click Refresh or enter them manually.
error.badCpu: CPU values must be numbers greater than 0
error.badMemory: Memory must be between 16M and 256G (for example 512M or 2G). 0M and oversized values are rejected.
error.badTag: Each tag must be versioned (vX.Y.Z / vX.Y.Z-rc.N), optionally @sha256:<64hex>. latest is not allowed.
error.netInvalid: {key} is not a valid Docker network name
error.netDuplicate: {prev} and {key} use the same Docker network name “{value}”. The names must differ.
error.netExtraClash: {key} and the additional Docker network use the same name “{value}”. The names must differ.
error.uploadNotText: The file could not be read as text
error.uploadNul: Binary files that contain NUL are rejected
error.uploadTooLong: The file exceeds the size limit
error.domainFormat: The primary domain is not valid. Use a hostname such as myriad.example.com.
error.extraFormat: The additional domain is not valid. Leave it empty if none is required.
error.dbHostStep: Enter the host of the external database
tags.loadingHub: Fetching the latest versioned tags from Docker Hub…
tags.aligned: all four components share the same version
tags.mismatch: component tags may differ; confirm compatibility
tags.resolved: Resolved: MYRIAD={myriad} · PROXY={proxy} · UPDATER={updater} · {align}{fail} (:latest is not allowed; production may add @sha256:…)
tags.failStatus: Fetch failed: {message}. Enter a versioned tag manually.
tags.hubEmpty: No usable versioned tag (vX.Y.Z) was found on Docker Hub{detail}
tags.hubUnavailable: This environment cannot reach Docker Hub
nginx.summary.defaultTemplate: Using the default Nginx template (nothing uploaded)
nginx.summary.rewroteLocation: Pointed location / at the Myriad proxy (full-site reverse proxy)
nginx.summary.injectedAcme: Injected a local ACME challenge root
nginx.summary.nginxTRequired: A handwritten parser cannot replace nginx -t. Run the check on the target host before going live.
panel.aapanel.desc: International Baota. Paste compose, or place the files in the site directory
panel.aapanel.wizardHint: After generation, paste the compose file, or place both files in the same directory.
panel.aapanel.label: aaPanel
panel.aapanel.siteStep2: Request SSL in the site settings
panel.aapanel.siteStep3: Drop the site configuration file below
panel.aapanel.resultsIntro: Paste YAML into Compose, or place compose and .env in the same directory. For the bundled database, read the directory permission notes first.
panel.portainer.desc: Paste compose into Stacks; keep .env in the same directory
panel.portainer.wizardHint: After generation, create a Portainer stack and place .env in the same directory.
panel.portainer.envBadge: Same directory as the stack · .env file
panel.portainer.label: Portainer
panel.portainer.siteStep1: Start the stack, then prepare an outer reverse proxy for {domain}
panel.portainer.siteStep3: If Nginx is used, drop the existing .conf below
panel.portainer.resultsIntro: Paste docker-compose.yml in Portainer → Stacks and place .env in the same directory. The outer proxy must cover the entire site.
panel.dockge.desc: Create a compose project in Dockge with .env in the same directory
panel.dockge.wizardHint: After generation, create a Dockge project and place both files in the same directory.
panel.dockge.label: Dockge
panel.dockge.siteStep1: Start the compose project, then prepare an outer reverse proxy for {domain}
panel.dockge.siteStep3: If Nginx is used, drop the existing .conf below
panel.dockge.resultsIntro: Create a Dockge compose project and place docker-compose.yml and .env in the same directory. The outer proxy must cover the entire site.
panel.coolify.desc: Deploy with Docker Compose; configure the domain and certificate in Coolify
panel.coolify.wizardHint: After generation, create a Coolify Compose service and attach the domain there.
panel.coolify.label: Coolify
panel.coolify.siteStep1: Create a Docker Compose service in Coolify
panel.coolify.siteStep3: Confirm full-site forwarding and WebSocket support
panel.coolify.resultsIntro: Paste docker-compose.yml in Coolify and set the environment variables. Coolify handles the domain, certificate, and reverse proxy; the entire site must be forwarded.
panel.dokploy.desc: Deploy with Compose; bind the site and issue a certificate under Domains
panel.dokploy.wizardHint: After generation, create a Dokploy Compose app and bind the site under Domains.
panel.dokploy.label: Dokploy
panel.dokploy.siteStep1: Create a Compose application in Dokploy
panel.dokploy.siteStep3: Confirm full-site forwarding and WebSocket support
panel.dokploy.resultsIntro: Paste docker-compose.yml in Dokploy and set the environment variables. Bind the site under Domains and forward the entire host.
panel.npm.desc: Start with compose, then create a Proxy Host in Nginx Proxy Manager
panel.npm.wizardHint: After generation, start the stack, then forward the domain to the local port in NPM.
panel.npm.label: Nginx Proxy Manager
panel.npm.siteStep2: Create a Proxy Host for {domain} pointing at the local port
panel.npm.siteStep3: Enable SSL, Force SSL, and WebSockets, and forward the entire site
panel.npm.resultsIntro: Start docker-compose.yml and .env first, then create a Proxy Host in Nginx Proxy Manager. Forward the entire site to the local port and enable WebSockets.
panel.caddy.desc: Start with compose and use Caddy in front for automatic HTTPS
panel.caddy.wizardHint: After generation, place both files in one directory and start, then use the generated Caddyfile.
panel.caddy.label: Caddy
panel.caddy.siteStep2: Give the generated Caddyfile to Caddy
panel.caddy.siteStep3: Confirm that Caddy listens on ports 80 and 443
panel.caddy.resultsIntro: Place docker-compose.yml and .env in the same directory and start, then use the generated Caddyfile for full-site reverse proxy and automatic HTTPS.
site.titlePlatform: Bind the domain in the platform
site.leadPlatform: These platforms provide a reverse proxy and certificates. Add the domain there and forward the entire site to Myriad, not /api only.
site.hintPlatform: No Nginx file is required. The domain, certificate, and reverse proxy are configured in the selected platform.
site.leadNpm: Start the stack first, then create a Proxy Host. Forward the entire site, enable WebSockets, and turn on SSL.
site.hintNpm: No Nginx file is required. The completion page explains how to fill in the Proxy Host.
site.leadCaddy: Start the stack first. A Caddyfile will be generated so Caddy can handle automatic HTTPS and the full-site reverse proxy.
site.hintCaddy: No Nginx file is required. The result includes a Caddyfile.
guide.aapanel.pasteTitle: Paste the compose file into aaPanel
guide.aapanel.pasteBody: Open aaPanel → Docker → Compose, create a stack, paste docker-compose.yml, and place .env in the same directory.
guide.aapanel.overwriteBody: Open Website → configuration and overwrite it with the generated {domain}.conf. The proxy target is {bind} and must cover the entire site /.
guide.portainer.pasteBody: Open Portainer → Stacks → Add stack, paste docker-compose.yml, and place .env in that stack directory.
guide.portainer.proxyBody: Place the generated {domain}.conf in Nginx, or use Caddy / NPM, and reverse-proxy the entire site to {bind}. Do not proxy /api only.
guide.dockge.pasteBody: Open Dockge, create a compose project, paste docker-compose.yml, and place .env in the same directory.
guide.dockge.proxyBody: Place the generated {domain}.conf in Nginx, or use Caddy / NPM, and reverse-proxy the entire site to {bind}. Do not proxy /api only.
guide.coolify.pasteTitle: Create a Compose service in Coolify
guide.coolify.pasteBody: Create a Docker Compose service, paste docker-compose.yml, and enter the environment variables from .env.
guide.coolify.domainBody: Add {domain} and enable HTTPS. Forward the entire site to {bind} and enable WebSockets. Do not forward /api only.
guide.dokploy.pasteTitle: Create a Compose app in Dokploy
guide.dokploy.pasteBody: Create a Compose application, paste docker-compose.yml, and set the environment variables.
guide.dokploy.domainBody: Add {domain} under Domains and enable a certificate. Forward the entire site to {bind} and enable WebSockets.
guide.npm.placeTitle: Place the files in one directory and start
guide.npm.placeBody: Create a directory on the server, add docker-compose.yml and .env, then run the command.
guide.npm.proxyTitle: Create a Proxy Host in NPM
guide.npm.proxyBody: Set Domain Names to the site domain. Forward to {bind} over http, and enable Websockets and SSL. Forward the entire site; do not forward /api only. If NPM and Myriad are not on the same network, use a reachable forward host.
guide.caddy.placeTitle: Place the files in one directory and start
guide.caddy.placeBody: Create a directory on the server, add docker-compose.yml and .env, then run the command.
guide.caddy.proxyBody: Give the generated Caddyfile to Caddy. reverse_proxy points at {bind} and covers the entire {domain} site. Run caddy validate.
nginx.summary.caddy: Generated a Caddyfile (automatic HTTPS, full-site reverse_proxy)
nginx.summary.platformProxy: The selected platform handles the reverse proxy and certificate; no Nginx file was generated
